hints.title: Reproduce it by hand
hints.content: Walk `paginate([1..7], 1, 3)` through the code line by line. Where does the returned slice start? For page 1 you want it to start at the very first item.

hints.title: Look at the start index
hints.content: The slice start is computed from `page * pageSize`. For page 1 that's `1 * pageSize`, so the whole first block is skipped. Pages are 1-indexed, but slice offsets are 0-indexed - those don't line up.

hints.title: Convert a 1-indexed page to a 0-indexed offset
hints.content: To turn a 1-indexed page number into a 0-indexed offset, subtract one before multiplying: the first item of page `p` lives at index `(p - 1) * pageSize`.

hints.title: The one-line fix
hints.content: Change the start index to `(page - 1) * pageSize` (in Python, `(page - 1) * page_size`). Page 1 now starts at 0 and page 2 at `pageSize`; the partial-last-page and past-the-end cases fall out of the slice bounds automatically.
